title: India's Retail Inflation Breaches RBI Ceiling at 6.09% as Food Prices Surge
excerpt: October's CPI reading, the highest since October 2024, crossed the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit as food inflation hit 8.94% and onion prices more than doubled, strengthening expectations of a second straight rate hike in December.
body:
• India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, breaching the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit for the first time under the new CPI series, MoSPI data showed on Thursday.
  • Food inflation accelerated to 8.94% from 7.74%, with onion prices up 116.22% year on year; rural inflation, at 6.63%, ran well above urban inflation of 5.41%.
  • The reading beat the 5.93% median forecast in a Reuters poll of economists and was the highest since October 2024's 6.2% under the previous series.
  • For households, the pressure is in the food basket; for borrowers and savers, economists now expect a second successive repo rate hike when the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee meets on December 2-4, after October's increase to 5.50%.

India's retail inflation surged to 6.09% in October, breaching the central bank's upper tolerance limit as rising food prices drove up household costs, according to data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation on Thursday and reported by The Hindu BusinessLine. The reading marks a 55-basis-point increase over September's 5.54% and the highest level since October 2024, when inflation stood at 6.21%.

The Reserve Bank of India's inflation-targeting framework mandates keeping CPI inflation at 4%, with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%. Inflation has now remained above the 4% medium-term target for five consecutive months, Reuters reported, and has increased for nine consecutive months, more than doubling from 2.74% in January.

Food Prices Did the Damage

The October jump was led by food. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index, accelerated to 8.94% in October from 7.74% in September, as prices of staples such as onions, garlic, and ginger climbed. Onion prices recorded inflation of 116.22% year on year, up from a 108.13% rise in September. The burden fell unevenly: rural inflation rose to 6.63% in October from 6.08% in September, against urban inflation of 5.41%, with food inflation at 9.09% in rural areas and 8.68% in urban areas.

What the RBI Does Next

The data lands six weeks after the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously on October 7 to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shift its stance to calibrated tightening. The RBI now expects inflation to average 6% in the October-December quarter and has raised its forecast for the current financial year to 5.2% from 5% earlier. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has warned that a weak monsoon and strong El Nino conditions pose risks to agriculture and rural demand.

"The data reinforces our expectation of a second successive rate hike in December."

— Radhika Rao, Senior Economist and Executive Director, DBS Bank, to IANS

Economists told IANS that with headline inflation yet to peak and an unfavourable base effect ahead, the central bank's quarterly projection is likely to be revised higher. The MPC's next meeting is scheduled for December 2-4. For Indian households, another hike would keep borrowing costs elevated into the new year; for NRI savers, it would support deposit rates even as the food basket at home gets more expensive.
